sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises as the share of the credit limit in use grows.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk rises from zero to two or more delinquencies.
The two drive each other: utilization matters far more for applicants with two delinquencies than for those with none.
Income is among the next most important features, and risk generally falls as income rises.
Length of credit history is also among the next most important features, and risk generally falls as the history gets longer.
Debt-to-income ratio has a weak effect, and risk increases with it.
Applicant age has a negligible share of importance, and the data do not settle whether the two application attributes, feature_a and feature_b, matter.
